newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Mobutu examined in a Moroccan military hospital.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu examined in a Moroccan military hospital.

text.p: Zaire's ailing former leader, Mobutu Sese Seko, underwent on Tuesday what a medical source described as an intensive medical examination at a Rabat military hospital as a result of "health complications".
Mobutu, 66, was moved on Monday night from the civilian Avicenne medical centre in the Moroccan capital to the nearby Mohamed V military hospital, the source said.

"Mobutu underwent on Tuesday an intensive medical examination due to health complications...At this stage it is difficult to draw a clear picture of the president's health outlook," the source told Reuters.
Reporters were not allowed access to the hospital compound.
Mobutu, who has been suffering from prostate cancer, was brought to the Moroccan capital from the northern Moroccan port of Tangier last week and was admitted to Avicenne's cardiology ward.
Morocco's official news agency MAP said earlier that he had suffered "serious bleeding complications" and had undergone "radiological vascular intervention" on Saturday morning.
"The operation passed in good conditions and the patient was well," the agency said, quoting an authorised medical source.
A senior doctor said: "French Professor Alain Laroche, who supervised the radiological vascular intrevention on Mobutu, left Morocco after he ended successfully his mission."
Moroccan officials were not available for comment.
Mobutu, his family and entourage had been staying at a hotel south of Rabat, near King Hassan's palace at Skhirat, since their arrival in Morocco last month.
But on June 18 they moved to Le Mirage hotel in the sea resort at Cap Spartel, about 20 km (12 miles) from Tangier.
Officials then said they expected Mobutu to spend up to six weeks there. Mobutu had asked for political asylum in Spain and Portugal but had received no response, the Moroccan press reported.
A Western diplomat said several initiatives were taken by Mobutu's family for his hospitalisation in France but received no reply.
Mobutu's entourage, which is composed of around 30 people, was still staying at Le Mirage hotel in northern Morocco.
